protected_before.party.yaml:
# A demonstration party, not affiliated with, endorsed by or speaking for any real authority it names.
# The party artefact (policy-composition ticket 11; ADR-0012/ADR-0013). One
# signed file declaring driftwood: its roles, its parents as party+kind+
# (name+)version, its own size/appetite, its selected baseline, and its
# overlay. Signed under the same gitsign tag as every other artefact this
# repo publishes -- no second mechanism (ADR-0012).
#
# `implementations` and `controls` below are checked, on every pull request,
# against this repo's own Flux pins by platform/party/party_artefact.py
# (called through the pinned `platform` dependency, in shift-left.yml): they
# must equal gitops/platform/platform-pin.yaml's and
# gitops/flux-system/gotk-sync-nist.yaml's own spec.ref.tag, minus the "v".
# The two `feed` entries (ico's penalty-schema, feeds' threat-register) had
# no Flux pin anywhere in this estate until 2026-09-04, so the check named
# both as unchecked rather than silently skipping them. They have pins now:
# gitops/flux-system/gotk-sync-ico.yaml and gotk-sync-feeds.yaml, plus
# gotk-sync-insurer.yaml for the quote (eco-system tickets 62 and 77), and
# the composing workflows read `ref:` out of them. party_artefact.py still
# does not grade a feed pin, on purpose: it compares a declared version to a
# pin's tag as equal strings, and a feed pin is declared by MAJOR here (`v3`,
# `v2`) against a publisher tag of the form `v3.0.0` or
# `threat-register/v2.0.0`. Resolving a major to the publisher's newest
# matching signed tag is the feed contract's rule and lives there, in the
# hub's verify/feed-contract and verify/branch-refs.
#
# 2026-08-28 (ADR-0019): the `pricing` and `threat` parent kinds became one
# `feed` kind carrying a `name` -- ico's schema is feed/penalty-schema, and
# the threat register's publisher moved from platform to the new `feeds`
# repo as feed/threat-register.
#
# 2026-08-28 (ADR-0021, ticket 25): driftwood also publishes now. Its twin
# emits a forward-intel feed from its own overlay in twin/, so `publisher`
# joins the roles and the feed gets a publishes[] record -- the set of signed
# publisher artefacts IS the catalogue (ADR-0019 point 5).
party: driftwood
roles: [risk-bearer, adopter, publisher]
reporting_currency: GBP
# This party's own signed size. The percent-of-turnover and per-subject
# formulas scale against these numbers, and the per-customer restatement of
# every prices[] entry divides by `customers` (ticket 25, ADR-0020). A stale
# `as_of` widens the loss triple to the statutory cap; it never refuses.
size:
  turnover: { amount: 86000000, currency: GBP }
  customers: 240000
  data_subjects: 240000
  headcount: 410
  as_of: '2026-06-30'
# The signed fact the tier selection reads (ADR-0021 point 5). It was
# platform/risk/appetite.json orgs.driftwood.tolerance; the platform's fixture
# is retired, because whose money is at risk is this party's own declaration
# and nobody else's. Loosest in the estate: Audit-heavy, short-life cart PII.
appetite:
  tolerance: { amount: 40000, currency: GBP }
# MODERATE: 287 controls, holds ac-6, cm-6 and ac-6.10. LOW excludes ac-6,
# one of the two controls this estate implements (ADR-0013). May add
# controls to this selection; may never remove one. Mirrored, advisory only,
# in gitops/apps/nist-pin-configmap.yaml's data.baselineName.
baseline: MODERATE
inherits:
  - { party: platform, kind: implementations, version: "4.0.0", since: '2026-08-28' }
  - { party: nist,     kind: controls,        version: "1.1.0", since: '2026-08-28' }
  - { party: ico,      kind: feed, name: penalty-schema,    version: "v3", since: '2026-08-28' }
  - { party: feeds,    kind: feed, name: threat-register,   version: "v2", since: '2026-08-28' }
  # The insurer's signed quote for THIS party, one feed name per adopter
  # (ticket 36; ticket 14 answers 3 and 4). It is the only parent whose price
  # is a COST rather than an exposure: composition books its premium into
  # prices[] as the `premium` kind under this party's own perspective, beside
  # costs.fix, and never sums it with the insurer's own layer arithmetic.
  # Renovate bumps this line when the insurer tags a re-quote.
  - { party: insurer,  kind: feed, name: quote-driftwood,    version: "v1", since: '2026-08-28' }
# What this party publishes and where it lives in this repo. The twin renders
# `twin/forward-intel/v1/feed.json` from `twin/orgs/driftwood/` with
# `twin/emit-forward-intel.py`; rule.yaml and bump.yaml sit beside it. Signed
# by the same gitsign tag as everything else here (ADR-0012), so an untagged
# feed.json on a branch is never a signature.
publishes:
  # The exposure section this repository's own composition renders into
  # composed/HEADER.yaml and signs under this repository's own tag. It is a
  # SECTION of a signed artefact, not an ADR-0019 envelope of its own, so it
  # declares no payload_schema and there is no <path>/v*/feed.json to read --
  # the tag is what signs it. Declared here because ADR-0019 point 5 makes
  # publishes[] the only discovery record there is, and the insurer pins this
  # exposure as a parent; without this record its pin resolved to nothing.
  - kind: feed
    name: exposure
    path: composed
    payload_schema: null
    revoked: []
  - kind: feed
    name: forward-intel
    path: twin/forward-intel
    payload_schema: twin/forward-intel/payload.schema.json
    revoked: []
overlay:
  add: []
  restate: []

protected_before.gitops/platform/platform-pin.yaml:
# driftwood consumes `platform` as a PINNED, SIGNED dependency (the config-base
# pattern, one level up): the same governance machinery is inherited, not
# copy-pasted. driftwood does not author policy versions — it pins a signed
# release of platform and lets Flux fan the version array out into this cluster.
#
# Opt-in, NOT wired into gitops/apps (whose Kustomization health-gates on
# wait: true) so it can't affect the Phase-0 reconcile beat. Apply it once the
# cluster has its prerequisites (see estate/platform/distribution/README.md):
#   * Kyverno       (the ValidatingPolicy CRDs the versions install)
#   * flux-operator (the ResourceSet CRD that fans the array out)
# then:  kubectl apply -k estate/driftwood/gitops/platform/
#
# Bump = one reviewed PR changing .spec.ref.tag (+commit) here — driftwood adopts
# a platform improvement on its own cadence.
apiVersion: source.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: GitRepository
metadata:
  name: platform
  namespace: flux-system
  annotations:
    # Ticket 41's identity-pinned gitsign-verifying controller reads these three. Flux's own
    # spec.verify cannot verify a gitsign tag (ADR-0023 D3, fluxcd/source-controller#1068), so
    # this controller verifies platform's tag; platform is a verified source only, so it gates nothing.
    # The regexp and issuer are the constants platform's own release.yml pins; the five-fact
    # sample re-reads them off the live object and grades fact 2 against them, so a boundary that
    # verified with somebody else's identity is observed false rather than merely 'verified'.
    policy-as-versioned.dev/gitsign-identity-regexp: ^https://github\.com/policy-as-versioned-platform/platform/\.github/workflows/cut-release\.yml@refs/heads/(main|release/[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.x)$
    policy-as-versioned.dev/gitsign-issuer: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
spec:
  interval: 1m
  url: https://github.com/policy-as-versioned-platform/platform
  ref:
    tag: v4.0.0
    commit: 557c1538fe022c784ea4ffb345c92d2e4b11fe71
    # commit pinned at release (belt-and-braces immutability, ADR-0001) --
    # the resolved SHA platform v1.1.0 tag points to, real as of policy-
    # composition tickets 09-17. Bumped by the Renovate customManager in this repo renovate.json
    # (git-refs datasource, both fields together) whenever platform ships a
    # newer tag -- never by hand, never a moving branch.

# ONE DOCUMENT, ON PURPOSE (ecosystem ticket 40, ticket 16 answer item Q5): this file is now the
# platform GitRepository and nothing else, so it can be applied on its own as a VERIFIED SOURCE
# with no second policy install behind it. The Kustomization that used to sit below it -- the one
# that fans platform's own version array out onto the cluster -- moved to
# platform-distribution.yaml beside it. `kubectl apply -k gitops/platform/` still applies both and
# is unchanged; the five-fact sample's ephemeral cluster applies only this file.
#
# Why it matters, found by running it: with platform's fan-out installed alongside driftwood's
# composed set, BOTH ResourceSets render a cluster-scoped ValidatingPolicy called
# policy-version-orphan-guard. Whichever applied last won, and fact 4 of the sample reported the
# live guard unequal to driftwood's own composed/orphan-guard.yaml -- two owners, one name. Q5's
# rationale ("the boundary stays observable with no second policy install") is exactly this.
protected_before.gitops/composed/composed-set.yaml:
# The composed set, installed from driftwood's OWN signed tag (ticket 16 answer item Q5).
#
# Until this file existed, nothing under gitops/ referenced composed/ at all: the adopter's
# Kustomization reconciled ./apps -- a namespace and two ConfigMaps -- and every policy object on
# kind-driftwood had been put there by `kubectl apply`. That is why the five-fact sample checks
# the Flux INVENTORY (fact 5) as well as the object's bytes (fact 4): a hand-applied object with
# the right name satisfies the weaker check and proves nothing about reconciliation.
#
# The shape is platform's own `distribution/versions.yaml`, one level down: ONE version array is
# the whole contract, and a ResourceSet ranges it into a Kustomization per version. One more
# Kustomization, `composed-machinery`, reconciles `./composed` itself, where the composition
# renders the platform machinery (the orphan guard and cage, the governed-namespace cages, their
# holds and report, the bottom-rung reach cage and the `cage-isolated` class they name) together
# with the `kustomization.yaml` that lists exactly those files (eco-system ticket 130). The
# machinery's CEL allow-lists are ranged by the composition from the platform's served array, so
# this array must be exactly the version directories the pinned tag carries: a version composed
# and not installed would be admitted by the orphan cage and caged by nothing.
# `scripts/render_composed.py reach` grades that, and every other way a composed object can miss
# the cluster, offline.
#
# What is different here, and deliberately so:
#
#   * the source is DRIFTWOOD's own repository at DRIFTWOOD's own signed tag. driftwood does not
#     install platform's tree; it installs the artefact its own composition rendered from
#     platform's and nist's signed parents (composed/HEADER.yaml records those parent SHAs, and
#     fact 3 of the sample checks the live platform and nist pins against them).
#   * the tag is v3.0.0, not the v1.0.0 in gitops/flux-system/gotk-sync.yaml. v1.0.0 predates
#     composed/ and does not carry the tree this reconciles. A self-pin bump is a reviewed PR that
#     moves tag and commit together (renovate.json's customManagers track nist and platform, not
#     the self-pin).
#   * there is no `spec.verify` here. Flux's GitRepository.spec.verify speaks OpenPGP, and one
#     signature -- the gitsign tag -- is the only one this estate has (ADR-0023, D3). Verification
#     at the source boundary is the identity-pinned gitsign-verifying controller of ticket 41,
#     which reads the three `gitsign-*` annotations above. Where that controller has not run,
#     nothing has looked at the signature, so fact 2 of the five-fact sample is observed NULL --
#     could-not-look, which is never a pass. Writing a `verify:` block that cannot verify a
#     gitsign tag would turn that honest could-not-look into a green that means nothing, and a
#     `verify:` block that CAN pass is a second signer, which D3 forbids -- so fact 2 grades a
#     source verified through `spec.verify` as observed FALSE.
#
# OPT-IN, exactly like gitops/platform/: not listed in gitops/apps/kustomization.yaml, whose
# Kustomization health-gates the Phase-0 reconcile with `wait: true` and would fail on any cluster
# without flux-operator's ResourceSet CRD. Apply it with:
#
#     kubectl apply -k gitops/composed/
#
# .github/workflows/drift-sample.yml does exactly that on its ephemeral cluster.
# ponytail: wiring this into gitops/apps so every adopter reconciles it unattended is ticket 42's
# widening, once tuppence and ludlow carry flux-operator too. The ceiling of leaving it opt-in is
# that the composed set is in force only where somebody applied this -- and the sample reports
# that as facts 3, 4 and 5 observed false, never as a skip.
---
apiVersion: source.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: GitRepository
metadata:
  name: driftwood-composed
  namespace: flux-system
  annotations:
    # Ticket 41's identity-pinned gitsign-verifying controller reads these three. Flux's own
    # spec.verify cannot verify a gitsign tag (ADR-0023 D3, fluxcd/source-controller#1068), so
    # this controller verifies driftwood's own tag and suspends the composed Kustomizations if it fails.
    # The regexp and issuer are the constants driftwood's own release.yml pins; the five-fact
    # sample re-reads them off the live object and grades fact 2 against them, so a boundary that
    # verified with somebody else's identity is observed false rather than merely 'verified'.
    policy-as-versioned.dev/gitsign-identity-regexp: ^https://github\.com/policy-as-versioned-driftwood/driftwood/\.github/workflows/cut-release\.yml@refs/heads/(main|release/[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.x)$
    policy-as-versioned.dev/gitsign-issuer: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
    policy-as-versioned.dev/gitsign-gates: flux-system/composed-v5-0-0,flux-system/composed-machinery
  labels:
    policy-as-versioned.dev/composed-for: driftwood
spec:
  interval: 1m
  url: https://github.com/policy-as-versioned-driftwood/driftwood
  ref:
    tag: v3.0.0
    commit: bf9889aa6a6d979c87a5633240a1447765d73503
    # The resolved SHA driftwood's own v3.0.0 tag points to (`git ls-remote origin 'refs/tags/v3.0.0^{}'`,
    # 2026-09-24). Belt-and-braces immutability, ADR-0001.
---
apiVersion: fluxcd.controlplane.io/v1
kind: ResourceSet
metadata:
  name: composed-set
  namespace: flux-system
  labels:
    policy-as-versioned.dev/composed-for: driftwood
spec:
  inputs:
    - versions:
        # The versions driftwood's composition rendered under composed/policies/ at the tag above. This
        # array is the adopter's contract: `scripts/render_composed.py` READS IT to decide what to
        # render offline, and `render_composed.py reach` refuses it unless it equals the version
        # directories the pinned tag carries and every machinery allow-list at that tag. Move it
        # in the same pull request that moves the tag.
        - { version: "5.0.0" }
        # v3.0.0 carries composed/policies/v5.0.0 only, and every machinery allow-list at that
        # tag admits 5.0.0 only. It was composed under platform v4.0.0, which retires policy 4.0.0
        # (owner-instructed 2026-09-24). Every workload driftwood declares moved its claim to
        # 5.0.0 before this tag (Phase B), so dropping 4.0.0 here leaves no claim uncaged.
        # Dropping it prunes the composed-v4-0-0 Kustomization's objects.
  resourcesTemplate: |
    << range $v := (index (inputs) "versions") >>
    ---
    apiVersion: kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
    kind: Kustomization
    metadata:
      name: composed-v<< $v.version | slugify >>
      namespace: flux-system
      labels:
        policy-as-versioned.dev/composed-for: driftwood
    spec:
      interval: 5m
      retryInterval: 1m
      timeout: 3m
      sourceRef:
        kind: GitRepository
        name: driftwood-composed
      path: ./composed/policies/v<< $v.version >>
      prune: true    # retire a version -> delete the array element -> its objects are pruned
      wait: true
    << end >>
    ---
    # The platform machinery at the composed/ root (eco-system ticket 130). Until this route
    # existed a policy-version-orphan-guard was written inline here, as a Deny ranged from the
    # array, because composed/ carried no kustomization.yaml and a Flux Kustomization cannot
    # select single files out of a directory that also holds HEADER.yaml and evidence.json. The
    # composition now renders that kustomization.yaml, listing exactly the machinery files, so
    # the machinery arrives as rendered and signed, not as a second hand-kept copy. The inline
    # guard is gone: two owners of one name is what ticket 40 Q5 removed, and the composed guard
    # is an Audit beside an orphan CAGE, where the inline one refused.
    apiVersion: kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
    kind: Kustomization
    metadata:
      name: composed-machinery
      namespace: flux-system
      labels:
        policy-as-versioned.dev/composed-for: driftwood
    spec:
      interval: 5m
      retryInterval: 1m
      timeout: 3m
      sourceRef:
        kind: GitRepository
        name: driftwood-composed
      path: ./composed
      prune: true
      wait: true
protected_before.gitops/engine/kyverno.yaml:
# The engine driftwood declares: hub ADR-0033 point 2, eco-system ticket 147.
#
# driftwood owns the Kyverno version it runs, and this file is the one place it says which. It is a
# plain declaration, not a Kubernetes manifest. Nothing applies this file, and no Flux
# Kustomization reconciles gitops/engine/. A cluster that runs an engine for driftwood installs it
# from this file, or, on a cluster another adopter owns, from the owner's file, which must declare
# the same engine:
#   the drift lane    .github/workflows/drift-sample.yml downloads install.url, checks it against
#                     install.sha256 and applies it server-side on its ephemeral cluster (two
#                     Kyverno CRDs are larger than a client-side apply can annotate).
#   kind-driftwood    the named demo cluster driftwood owns. Hub talk/up.sh installs Kyverno on it
#                     from this file, through hub talk/engine-up.sh, the same way. tuppence's
#                     workload flagship runs there too, so tuppence must declare the same engine,
#                     and hub verify/adopter-engines asserts that.
#   the offline CLI   .github/workflows/shift-left.yml installs cli.linux_x86_64 by its sha256
#                     and refuses a binary that reports another version.
# .github/scripts/engine_declaration.py is the one reader in this repository, and it checks the
# shape. Eco-system ticket 161 builds verify-cage-probe.sh to read `version` from here as well.
#
# EVERY FIGURE is the row for this version in platform engine/kyverno/engine-table.yaml, which
# says where each came from: the CLI sha256 from the release's own checksums.txt, and the
# install.yaml sha256 from the GitHub release API's asset digest (checksums.txt does not list
# install.yaml). Hub verify/adopter-engines holds this file to that row on platform origin/main.
# The figures are carried here, and not read from the table, because the platform tools tag this
# repository pins (.github/platform-tools-pin.yaml, v4.0.0) predates the table.
#
# WHAT IT INSTALLS, measured 2026-09-26 on the bytes install.sha256 names: 70 objects. The 24
# namespaced ones (4 Deployments, 6 Services, 4 ServiceAccounts, 4 Roles, 4 RoleBindings and
# 2 ConfigMaps) all sit in the `kyverno` Namespace, which the platform declares as substrate
# (engine/namespaces.yaml, `posture.acme.io/tier: infra`). The other 46 are cluster-scoped: the
# Namespace itself, 22 CRDs, 16 ClusterRoles and 7 ClusterRoleBindings. Composition prices none
# of them: it walks this repository's own files, and this file declares no object.
#
# TO MOVE THE ENGINE: one reviewed pull request that changes the version and every figure
# together, from the engine table's row for the new version, and recomposes. Ticket 150 is the
# only ticket that moves an adopter's engine.
schema: 1
engine: kyverno
version: "1.18.2"
install:
  url: https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/releases/download/v1.18.2/install.yaml
  sha256: "3dcd43eaf11f0719084217148cd0c82a8fa49faa9b1a783ea5bea2cf84041bda"
cli:
  linux_x86_64:
    file: kyverno-cli_v1.18.2_linux_x86_64.tar.gz
    sha256: "cb2feb8356149fd2fe774c894ccf0969f4a60a83867dd913af724f74ffbbc18b"

# the same engine:

#                     Kyverno CRDs are larger than a client-side apply can annotate).

#                     owns. Hub talk/up.sh installs that cluster's Kyverno from driftwood's own
#                     gitops/engine/kyverno.yaml. One cluster runs one engine, so this file must
#                     declare the same engine as driftwood's, and hub verify/adopter-engines
#                     asserts that.

#                     and refuses a binary that reports another version.

# shape. Eco-system ticket 161 builds verify-cage-probe.sh to read `version` from here as well.
#
# EVERY FIGURE is the row for this version in platform engine/kyverno/engine-table.yaml, which
# says where each came from: the CLI sha256 from the release's own checksums.txt, and the
# install.yaml sha256 from the GitHub release API's asset digest (checksums.txt does not list
# install.yaml). Hub verify/adopter-engines holds this file to that row on platform origin/main.
# The figures are carried here, and not read from the table, because the platform tools tag this
# repository pins (.github/platform-tools-pin.yaml, v4.0.0) predates the table.
#
# WHAT IT INSTALLS, measured 2026-09-26 on the bytes install.sha256 names: 70 objects. The 24
# namespaced ones (4 Deployments, 6 Services, 4 ServiceAccounts, 4 Roles, 4 RoleBindings and
# 2 ConfigMaps) all sit in the `kyverno` Namespace, which the platform declares as substrate

# A demonstration party, not affiliated with, endorsed by or speaking for any real authority it names.
# The party artefact (policy-composition ticket 11; ADR-0012/ADR-0013).
# Same shape driftwood's copy documents in full -- see that repo's

# other artefact this repo publishes -- no second mechanism.

# whose roles do not say publisher is a record no resolver will look at.

reporting_currency: GBP

  tolerance: { amount: 5000, currency: GBP }

inherits:

  - { party: ico,      kind: feed, name: penalty-schema,    version: "v3", since: '2026-08-28' }
  - { party: feeds,    kind: feed, name: threat-register,   version: "v1", since: '2026-08-28' }
  # Eco-system ticket 84: the EOL feed the feeds publisher carries (eol/v2, the newest
  # directory it publishes). Priced through platform's converter as the feed's headline
  # component, ramped to the composition's own as-of date. The publisher has cut no
  # eol/vX.Y.Z tag yet, so until it does this pin is an untagged pin -- a PRICED HOLE of the
  # whole line under this party's own perspective (ticket 69), never a refusal. v2 rather than
  # v1 because two feeds of one publisher at one major share a vendored directory (ticket 45
  # refuses that), and v2 is what a subscriber joining today would pin. Renovate bumps this
  # line when a newer major is tagged; a supersede line (ticket 84) prices staying behind.
  - { party: feeds,    kind: feed, name: eol,               version: "v2", since: '2026-09-08' }
overlay:
  add: []
  restate: []
publishes:
  # The exposure section this repository's own composition renders into
  # composed/HEADER.yaml and signs under this repository's own tag. It is a
  # SECTION of a signed artefact, not an ADR-0019 envelope of its own, so it
  # declares no payload_schema and there is no <path>/v*/feed.json to read --

  - kind: feed

    revoked: []

    policy-as-versioned.dev/gitsign-issuer: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
    policy-as-versioned.dev/gitsign-gates: flux-system/composed-v5-0-0,flux-system/composed-machinery
  labels:
    policy-as-versioned.dev/composed-for: ludlow
spec:
  interval: 1m
  url: https://github.com/policy-as-versioned-ludlow/ludlow
  ref:
    tag: v3.0.0
    commit: 45b3fbd21d2838f8882dfa6265b3a6e8fa61b3a9
    # The resolved SHA ludlow's own v3.0.0 tag points to (`git ls-remote origin 'refs/tags/v3.0.0^{}'`,
    # 2026-09-24). Belt-and-braces immutability, ADR-0001.
---
apiVersion: fluxcd.controlplane.io/v1
kind: ResourceSet
metadata:
  name: composed-set
  namespace: flux-system
  labels:
    policy-as-versioned.dev/composed-for: ludlow
spec:
  inputs:
    - versions:
        # The versions ludlow's composition rendered under composed/policies/ at the tag above. This
        # array is the adopter's contract: `scripts/render_composed.py` READS IT to decide what to
        # render offline, and `render_composed.py reach` refuses it unless it equals the version
        # directories the pinned tag carries and every machinery allow-list at that tag. Move it
        # in the same pull request that moves the tag.
        - { version: "5.0.0" }
        # v3.0.0 carries composed/policies/v5.0.0 only. It was composed under platform v4.0.0,
        # which retired policy 4.0.0 (owner-instructed 2026-09-24), so 4.0.0 left this array in
        # the same pull request that moved the tag. The workloads ludlow declares claim 5.0.0.
  resourcesTemplate: |
    << range $v := (index (inputs) "versions") >>
    ---
    apiVersion: kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
    kind: Kustomization
    metadata:
      name: composed-v<< $v.version | slugify >>
      namespace: flux-system
      labels:
        policy-as-versioned.dev/composed-for: ludlow
    spec:
      interval: 5m
      retryInterval: 1m
      timeout: 3m
      sourceRef:
        kind: GitRepository
        name: ludlow-composed
      path: ./composed/policies/v<< $v.version >>
      prune: true    # retire a version -> delete the array element -> its objects are pruned
      wait: true
    << end >>
    ---
    # The platform machinery at the composed/ root (eco-system ticket 130). Until this route
    # existed a policy-version-orphan-guard was written inline here, as a Deny ranged from the
    # array, because composed/ carried no kustomization.yaml and a Flux Kustomization cannot
    # select single files out of a directory that also holds HEADER.yaml and evidence.json. The
    # composition now renders that kustomization.yaml, listing exactly the machinery files, so
    # the machinery arrives as rendered and signed, not as a second hand-kept copy. The inline
    # guard is gone: two owners of one name is what ticket 40 Q5 removed, and the composed guard
    # is an Audit beside an orphan CAGE, where the inline one refused.
    apiVersion: kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
    kind: Kustomization
    metadata:
      name: composed-machinery
      namespace: flux-system
      labels:
        policy-as-versioned.dev/composed-for: ludlow
    spec:
      interval: 5m
      retryInterval: 1m
      timeout: 3m
      sourceRef:
        kind: GitRepository
        name: ludlow-composed
      path: ./composed
      prune: true
      wait: true

#
# ludlow owns the Kyverno version it runs, and this file is the one place it says which. It is a
# plain declaration, not a Kubernetes manifest. Nothing applies this file, and no Flux

# from this file, or, on a cluster another adopter owns, from the owner's file, which must declare
# the same engine:
#   the drift lane    .github/workflows/drift-sample.yml downloads install.url, checks it against
#                     install.sha256 and applies it server-side on its ephemeral cluster (two
#                     Kyverno CRDs are larger than a client-side apply can annotate).
#   kind-ludlow       runs no engine, and ticket 147 adds none (hub ticket 71, decision 17).
#   the offline CLI   .github/workflows/shift-left.yml installs cli.linux_x86_64 by its sha256
#                     and refuses a binary that reports another version.
# .github/scripts/engine_declaration.py is the one reader in this repository, and it checks the
# shape. Eco-system ticket 161 builds verify-cage-probe.sh to read `version` from here as well.
#

# says where each came from: the CLI sha256 from the release's own checksums.txt, and the
# install.yaml sha256 from the GitHub release API's asset digest (checksums.txt does not list

# The figures are carried here, and not read from the table, because the platform tools tag this
# repository pins (.github/platform-tools-pin.yaml, v4.0.0) predates the table.
#

# 2 ConfigMaps) all sit in the `kyverno` Namespace, which the platform declares as substrate

# Namespace itself, 22 CRDs, 16 ClusterRoles and 7 ClusterRoleBindings. Composition prices none
# of them: it walks this repository's own files, and this file declares no object.
